paras: The dynamiting of Fannie Robinson's house was an attack on the home of a Black woman in Christiansburg, Virginia, at about 2 a.m. on March 20, 1903. Dynamite placed on the front door step partly demolished the house, but Robinson and her children, asleep inside, escaped unhurt. No one was identified as responsible, and the attack was reported only briefly in two white newspapers.

According to a special dispatch from Christiansburg, a "most terrific explosion" woke the town at 2 o'clock in the morning of March 20. Someone had placed dynamite on the front door step of the house of Fannie Robinson, described as "a colored woman," and the blast partially demolished the building. Robinson and her children were asleep in the house, and the correspondent called their escape without injury "almost miraculous." The damage to the house was estimated at either $100 or $500; the figure is unclear in the surviving print.

The dispatch reported "no clue" to the perpetrators, and Robinson said she could not even form a suspicion of who had done it. No report of an arrest, investigation or later follow-up appears in the coverage.

The Richmond Times-Dispatch carried the fullest account on March 21 under the headline "WITH DYNAMITE," with the subhead "Christiansburg is Startled at Night by Terrific Explosion." The story centered on the noise and the family's narrow escape and offered no motive for the attack. Two days later The Washington Times reduced it to a single unnamed line in its "Throughout the State" column of Virginia news, dating the explosion to "yesterday morning." No coverage in the Black press was found.

The Washington Times wording would place the explosion on March 22, but the Times-Dispatch report, dated from Christiansburg on March 20 and describing the blast as that morning, is the closer source.

bases: Dynamite placed on the front door step of a Black woman's occupied house partly demolished it; no attackers were identified and no one was hurt (A1, A2).

Only the Times-Dispatch special gives the details (A1); the Washington Times roundup line confirms a dynamite explosion at a colored woman's house in Christiansburg but is a condensed state-news item that is probably drawn from Virginia papers rather than an independent report (A2).
